notice: Paraphrased summaries for prototyping only. Verify every entry against the official document and obtain clinician sign-off before field use.

entries.title: Very severe disease in young infants

source.document: Management of the sick young infant aged up to 2 months: IMCI chart booklet

entries.summary: A young infant with any one of these signs is classified as having very severe disease: not feeding well, convulsions, fast breathing (60 or more breaths per minute) in an infant under 7 days old, severe chest indrawing, fever (37.5 °C or above), low body temperature (below 35.5 °C), or movement only when stimulated or no movement at all.
entries.action: Classified for urgent referral to hospital, with pre-referral care given by a trained health worker as the guideline describes.

entries.title: Fast breathing in infants aged 7-59 days

source.document: Management of the sick young infant aged up to 2 months: IMCI chart booklet

entries.summary: Fast breathing (60 or more per minute) as the only sign in an infant aged 7-59 days is classified as pneumonia, which a trained health worker may manage as an outpatient with close follow-up. In an infant under 7 days old it is a sign of very severe disease.
entries.action: Needs clinician assessment the same day. This prototype tells the ASHA to refer; the doctor decides management.

entries.title: Local bacterial infection of the umbilicus or skin

source.document: Management of the sick young infant aged up to 2 months: IMCI chart booklet

entries.summary: An umbilicus that is red or draining pus, or skin pustules, is classified as local bacterial infection when no sign of very severe disease is present.
entries.action: Managed by a trained health worker according to the guideline, with home-care advice and a follow-up visit.

entries.title: Spreading umbilical redness or many skin pustules

source.publisher: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
source.document: Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) chart booklet

entries.summary: India's IMNCI chart booklet treats umbilical redness extending to the skin, or 10 or more skin pustules or a big boil, as signs of possible serious bacterial infection.
entries.action: Urgent referral to a facility as the IMNCI chart booklet describes.

entries.title: Jaundice in young infants

source.document: Management of the sick young infant aged up to 2 months: IMCI chart booklet

entries.summary: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life, or yellow palms and soles at any age, is classified as severe jaundice. Jaundice without these features is managed with home-care advice and follow-up.
entries.action: Severe jaundice: urgent referral. Otherwise advise the family, follow up, and return immediately if the palms or soles turn yellow.

entries.title: Keeping a sick young infant safe during referral

source.publisher: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
source.document: Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) operational guidelines

entries.summary: When a sick newborn is referred, keep the baby warm (skin-to-skin contact with the mother), continue breastfeeding if the baby is able to feed, and arrange transport to the referral facility without delay.
entries.action: Arrange government referral transport where available (for example 102 or 108) and inform the receiving facility.

entries.title: Home-based newborn care visits by ASHAs

source.publisher: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
source.document: Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) operational guidelines

entries.summary: ASHAs make scheduled home visits during the first six weeks of life to check the newborn for danger signs, support breastfeeding and warmth, and refer sick newborns.
entries.action: Continue scheduled visits and teach the family the danger signs that need immediate care.
